Table 5.3: A Comparison between the Behaviour of Chromosomes and Genes
A
Occur in pairs
Segregate at the time of gamete formation such that only one of each pair is transmitted to a gamete
Independent pairs segregate independently of each other
B
Occur in pairs
Segregate at gamete formation and only one of each pair is transmitted to a gamete
One pair segregates independently of another pair
Can you tell which of these columns A or B represent the chromosome and which represents the gene? How did you decide?
italic_terms: Can you tell which of these columns A or B represent the chromosome and which represents the gene? How did you decide?

blocks.text: During Anaphase of meiosis I, the two chromosome pairs can align at the metaphase plate independently of each other (Figure 5.9). To understand this, compare the chromosomes of four different colour in the left and right columns. In the left column (Possibility I) orange and green is segregating together. But in the right hand column (Possibility II) the orange chromosome is segregating with the red chromosomes.

note: Reading order on the page is Table 5.3, its shaded question row, the prose paragraph, then Figure 5.9; the text layer stores the figure labels and caption first, which is the known layer-order artifact.
